PROOF.L0_DEGREE: Cell domain as in the T270 result: 22 triple labels + 27 pair labels cover 1..49, so every number has frequency 2 or 3; overlap <= 1 makes the numbers of a ticket reach disjoint neighbour sets, so deg(v) = 6 + t(v). Profile 5^12 1^6 0^2 gives degrees 11^12, 7^6, 6^2, |E| = 93. The argument below uses only the overlap graph G, so it excludes every simple graph with these degrees, whether or not it is realised by tickets.
PROOF.P1_S1_WEDGES: W = 12*55 + 6*21 + 2*15 = 816. Each triangle closes exactly 3 wedges and each closed wedge lies in exactly one triangle, so O = W - 3T = 816 - 807 = 9 at T = 269.
PROOF.P1_S2_EDGE_IDENTITY: For an edge uv the open wedges with arm uv are: centre u, other end w in N(u)-{v}, w not in N(v), numbering (deg u - 1) - |N(u)&N(v)|; symmetrically for centre v. An open wedge has exactly two arms, so sum over edges of [deg u + deg v - 2 - 2|N(u)&N(v)|] = 2O = 18, every summand >= 0.
PROOF.P1_S3_HL_BOUND: H = the 12 degree-11 vertices, L = the other 8, c = e(H,L). For an edge uv with u in H, v in L: N(u)&N(v) is a subset of N(v)-{u}, so |N(u)&N(v)| <= deg v - 1, and the two terms sum to (10 - k) + (deg v - 1 - k) >= 11 - deg v >= 4 for deg v in {6,7}, k = |N(u)&N(v)|. Dropping the other (nonnegative) summands: 4c <= 18, so c <= 4.
PROOF.P1_S4_PARITY: sum_{u in H} deg u = 132 = 2e(H) + c, so c is even: c in {0, 2, 4}. Then e(H) = 66, 65, 64 and e(L) = (54 - c)/2 = 27, 26, 25.
PROOF.P1_S5_C0: c = 0: e(H) = 66 = C(12,2) so G[H] = K12; e(L) = 27 = C(8,2) - 1 so G[L] = K8 - e, and the degrees 7^6 6^2 force e to join the two degree-6 vertices. G = K12 disjoint-union (K8 - e), T = C(12,3) + (C(8,3) - 6) = 220 + 50 = 270 != 269. No graph with c = 0 has T = 269.
PROOF.P1_S6_C2: c = 2: e(H) = 65 = C(12,2) - 1, so exactly one pair x,y in H is non-adjacent, and each of the other 10 vertices of H is adjacent to both: 10 distinct open wedges x-z-y with all three vertices in H (x,y non-adjacent in G because adjacency inside H is G[H]). O >= 10 > 9, a contradiction.
PROOF.P1_S7_C4: c = 4: e(H) = 64 = C(12,2) - 2, so G[H] is K12 minus two edges. Adjacent missing edges ab, ac: the non-adjacent pairs are {a,b} and {a,c}; for {a,b} the 9 vertices outside {a,b,c} are adjacent to both (c is not adjacent to a), likewise for {a,c}: 9 + 9 = 18 open wedges. Disjoint missing edges ab, cd: {a,b} has all 10 other H vertices adjacent to both, likewise {c,d}: 10 + 10 = 20. Wedges with different end pairs are different wedges, so no wedge is counted twice. O >= 18 > 9 in both sub-cases, a contradiction.
PROOF.P1_S8_RESULT: c in {0,2,4} are the only possibilities (S3, S4); c = 0 gives T = 270 exactly, c = 2 and c = 4 give O >= 10 and O >= 18, i.e. T <= 268 and T <= 266. Hence no graph with degrees 11^12 7^6 6^2 has T = 269: the cell is empty.
